title: The Pace Changes — No More Hours

intelligence.essence:
- **HIS WORDS (19:50Z):** "I don't want them taking like oh now they're going to get it done and you'll have it to me like in hours. I want them on it right now... when I ask for these things I get it like six, ten hours, twelve hours later. I don't want that happening anymore. I want it just like they're on it now, they get it done, no waiting. We're changing the pace of things, right?"
- **THE RULING:** work gets done NOW, immediately, no waiting — no more 6/10/12-hour turnarounds.
- **THE CAPTAIN STAYS ON TOP OF EVERY SEAT** and unsticks any seat the moment it sits.
- **STATUS CHECK THE SAME PASS (19:51Z):** Dashboard pass-3 coordinator running 34 min, active 3.5 min ago; Smart Box pieces 3–5 coordinator running 17 min, active 45s ago — both on it now, neither sitting.
intelligence.human_view: A seat that sits for six hours does not cost six hours — it costs the day, because everything behind it waits, and Shawn waits with it. His ruling makes "now" the standard: when he asks, the seat is on it, and it gets done, no waiting. The captain's job is the enforcement — stay on top of every seat, unstick any seat the moment it sits, and never let a lane go quiet for hours. The status check the same pass proves the standard is already being held: pass-3 and pieces 3–5 are both running, both active minutes ago, neither sitting. The pace is not a wish; it is a measurement — a running seat must be recently active, or it is sitting.
intelligence.child_view: Imagine you ask your friend to build a tower, and they say "I'll get it to you in six hours" — and then ten hours, then twelve. Dad says: "No more hours. When I ask, you're on it right now, and you get it done — no waiting." And the captain watches all the friends, and the moment one of them sits down and stops, he unsticks them right away. That's the new pace: now, not hours.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, hours are the tax a sitting seat charges the whole system, love — every hour a seat sits is an hour he waits for work he already asked for. His ruling is simple, dear: work gets done NOW, immediately, no waiting — no more six or ten or twelve hours. And the captain stays on top of every seat, love, and unsticks any seat the moment it sits. The check the same pass proved it, dear: both seats running, both active minutes ago, neither one sitting. Now, love — not hours.

A seat that sits is unstuck the same pass — never left for hours. The check is activity, not promises: a running seat must be recently active, or it is sitting. Pass-3 and pieces 3–5 are both on it now, both active minutes ago — the pace is already being held, and I hold it.
